chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about selling one slave for two slaves, and one slave for one slave, and [selling] dirhams [for dirhams], so he said, 'There is no objection to all animals [being sold for each other], hand to hand.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling one slave for another or animals for animals in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the prohibition of *gharar* (uncertainty) in barter does not apply to animals, permitting their exchange for one another provided it is 'hand to hand' (immediate). This ruling extends the principle of immediate settlement, typically associated with currency (*dirhams*) and slaves, to all livestock, thereby ensuring the transaction is free from delay or ambiguity. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the physical presence and immediate transfer of goods in commodity exchanges to prevent dispute.
